name: Redvale
region_detail: On both banks of the Redwash in the western central grasslands, connected by wagon roads to Cador and the other marquisates.
site_type: settlement | Inhabited locations | Ranching and livestock market town; administrative seat of the Marquisate of Redvale.
history: The Redwash ford was a customary watering and trading place for Varkesh and Rathen herders, visited by Thalenweald merchants and Qasari caravans. A Cadorian trading post grew around the crossing. Garrus Ashford chose Redvale as his seat after the Edict of the East in 3E-991.
current_state: In 3E-992 the unwalled town is expanding rapidly. Stockyards, warehouses, new roads, and ranching concessions support the livestock trade. Four-Spur’s growing influence and fencing of customary grazing lands threaten independent ranchers and herding communities. The sheriff retains a measure of independence from the marquis.
inhabitants: Ranchers, drovers, horse breeders, merchants, settlers, laborers, Copper Spurs, and visiting Varkesh, Rathen, Thalenweald, and Qasari traders.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; localized brawls, stock disputes, and criminal activity. Armed confrontations may develop over grazing and water rights outside town.
points_of_interest:
Spur Street; Old Ford and Water Bell; Stockyards; Ashford Rise and Copper Spurs headquarters; Dry End; Last Water; Redwash Exchange; Four-Spur Yards; Overland Depot; Sixth Bolt; Tall Lantern; Open Table; sheriff’s office.

Unresolved elements: Exact map hex; local street plan and building layouts; opening job and rumor selections; the progression of disputes over water, livestock, and land.
discovery: On both banks of the Redwash in the western central grasslands, connected by wagon roads to Cador and the other marquisates. Known throughout the frontier. Wagon roads connect the town to the Great Eastway, Blackvein, and Westbridge; customary trails extend toward desert-margin wells.
